literal: Moqi Pu; son Luo; Kezhuhun Yuan; Liu Feng; Poliuhan Chang; Jin Zuo; Wei Zican
idiomatic: Moqi Pu; his son Luo; Kezhuhun Yuan; Liu Feng; Poliuhan Chang; Jin Zuo; Wei Zican

literal: Moqi Pu, styled Pubo, was a native of Taiping; his ancestors were a separate branch of the Xiongnu.
idiomatic: Moqi Pu, styled Pubo, came from Taiping; his forebears were a separate branch of the Xiongnu.

literal: Bold and resolute, he had martial strength.
idiomatic: He was bold and resolute and possessed martial strength.

literal: In the Zhenguang era, Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Pu was appointed Grand Mentor.
idiomatic: In the Zhenguang era Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Pu was appointed grand mentor.

literal: He led his tribe in surrender to Wei and was appointed General of the Rear Guard and second leader of the tribal chieftains.
idiomatic: He led his tribe in surrender to Wei and was made general of the rear guard and second leader of the tribal chieftains.

literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous standard, Pu sent pledges of loyalty from afar; Gao Huan greatly praised him.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous standard, Pu sent pledges of loyalty from afar; Gao Huan greatly praised him.

literal: When Husu Chun forced the emperor westward, Pu was appointed Minister of Works and inspector of Qin Province, holding Fuche City.
idiomatic: When Husu Chun forced the emperor westward, Pu was appointed minister of works and inspector of Qin Province, holding Fuche City.

literal: When Gao Huan pacified Xia Province, Pu then led his tribe to come and submit; Gao Huan personally went out to receive him and appointed Pu Duke of Hexi.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan pacified Xia Province, Pu led his tribe to submit; Gao Huan went out in person to receive him and made him duke of Hexi.

literal: He rose in repeated promotions to Grand Mentor and inspector of Shuozhou, then died.
idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to grand mentor and inspector of Shuozhou, then died.

literal: His son Luo, styled Shouluogan.
idiomatic: His son Luo, styled Shouluogan.

literal: Bold and stalwart, skilled in martial arts; his mounted archery surpassed others, and the village community respected him.
idiomatic: Bold and stalwart, skilled in the martial arts; his mounted archery surpassed others, and the village community respected him.

literal: When Baling rebelled, he followed his father in submitting; he was appointed Manifest Martial General.
idiomatic: When Baling rebelled he followed his father in submitting and was appointed manifest martial general.

literal: Following Erzhu Rong he had battle merit in every engagement; he rose in successive promotions to inspector of Fenzhou and General of Agile Cavalry.
idiomatic: Following Erzhu Rong he won merit in every battle; he rose in successive promotions to inspector of Fenzhou and general of agile cavalry.

literal: When the righteous rising began at Xindu, he sent pledges of loyalty from afar; Gao Huan praised that father and son had both come and treated them with exceptional courtesy.
idiomatic: When the righteous rising began at Xindu he sent pledges of loyalty from afar; Gao Huan praised that father and son had both come and treated them with exceptional courtesy.

literal: He was appointed Pacification Army [commander] and concurrently inspector of Ling Province.
idiomatic: He was appointed to the Pacification Army and concurrently made inspector of Ling Province.

literal: When Emperor Wu entered the passes, he was appointed Vice Director of the Left.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu entered the passes he was appointed left vice director.

literal: In the Tianping era he followed his father east; he was enfeoffed Duke of Jianchang commandery and promoted again to Commander of the Guards.
idiomatic: In the Tianping era he followed his father east; he was enfeoffed duke of Jianchang commandery and promoted again to commander of the guards.

literal: With the generals he besieged Dugu Ruyuan at Jinyong; at the battle of Heyin he had merit as well.
idiomatic: With the generals he besieged Dugu Ruyuan at Jinyong; at the battle of Heyin he had merit as well.

literal: Gao Huan, because his father Pu was honored as an elder, especially elevated his ritual treatment; he once personally helped him mount his horse.
idiomatic: Because his father Pu was honored as an elder, Gao Huan especially elevated his ritual treatment; he once personally helped him mount his horse.

literal: Luo removed his cap and performed the forehead knock, saying: "I wish to give my utmost strength to repay your deep grace.
idiomatic: Luo removed his cap and performed the forehead knock, saying: "I wish to give my utmost strength to repay your deep grace.

literal: " And in this battle, when the armies crossed the bridge northward, Luo held one army motionless.
idiomatic: " In this battle, when the armies crossed the bridge northward, Luo held one army motionless.

literal: He said to the westerners: "Moqi Shouluogan is here — if you can come, come!
idiomatic: He said to the westerners: "Moqi Shouluogan is here — if you can come, come!

literal: " The westerners feared and departed.
idiomatic: " The westerners feared him and withdrew.

literal: Gao Huan, because of his heroism and stature, named the place he camped Huiluo City.
idiomatic: Because of his heroism and stature, Gao Huan named the place he camped Huiluo City.

literal: Luo was generous and had moral resolve; his courage and sharpness crowned the age; his contemporaries esteemed him a famous general.
idiomatic: Luo was generous and high-minded; his courage and keenness crowned the age, and his contemporaries esteemed him a famous general.

literal: He died early in Xinghe.
idiomatic: He died early in the Xinghe era.

literal: Kezhuhun Yuan, styled Daoyuan.
idiomatic: Kezhuhun Yuan, styled Daoyuan.

literal: He himself said he was from Liaodong.
idiomatic: He himself said he was from Liaodong.

literal: For generations his family had been tribal chiefs; in Wei times they led their masses in submission; his great-grandfather Huyegu ended as general of Huaishuo garrison, and the family settled there.
idiomatic: For generations his family had been tribal chiefs; in Wei times they led their followers in submission; his great-grandfather Huyegu died as general of Huaishuo garrison, and the family settled there.

literal: Yuan was broad and benevolent, with military strategy; in youth he knew Gao Huan well.
idiomatic: Yuan was broad-minded and benevolent, with military strategy; in youth he knew Gao Huan well.

literal: When the north border was in turmoil, he led his household to go to Dingzhou; they encountered Xianyu Xiuli raising rebellion, and Yuan led his masses to join him.
idiomatic: When the northern frontier was in turmoil he led his household to Dingzhou; they encountered Xianyu Xiuli raising rebellion, and Yuan led his followers to join him.

literal: Ge Rong swallowed up Xiuli, and again made Yuan Prince of Liang.
idiomatic: Ge Rong swallowed up Xiuli and again made Yuan prince of Liang.

literal: He then fled to Erzhu Rong, who made him a separate commander; he was attached to Tian Guang's campaign into Guanzhong, and for merit was made inspector of Wei Province.
idiomatic: He then fled to Erzhu Rong, who made him a separate commander; he was attached to Tian Guang's campaign into Guanzhong and, for merit, was made inspector of Wei Province.

literal: When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, Yuwen Tai led Yue's troops back and together they plotted against Yue.
idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, Yuwen Tai led Yue's troops back and together they plotted against Yue.

literal: At that time Yuan helped Yue; when Yue fled, Yuan gathered his troops, entered and held Qinzhou, was besieged by Zhou, fought bitterly, and made an alliance to cease.
idiomatic: At that time Yuan helped Yue; when Yue fled, Yuan gathered his troops, entered and held Qinzhou, was besieged by Zhou forces, fought bitterly, and made an alliance to cease hostilities.

literal: Yuan had early been known and favored by Gao Huan; moreover his mother and elder brother were in the east; he always had thoughts of returning home, constantly sent memorials, and secretly corresponded with Gao Huan.
idiomatic: Yuan had long been known and favored by Gao Huan; moreover his mother and elder brother were in the east; he always yearned to return, constantly sent memorials, and secretly corresponded with Gao Huan.

literal: Yuwen Tai feared Yuan's wisdom and courage, knew Yuan was of two minds, and sent troops to attack him.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai feared Yuan's wisdom and courage, knew Yuan was of two minds, and sent troops to attack him.

literal: Yuan then led his division, setting out from Wei Province, and crossed Wulan ford northwestward.
idiomatic: Yuan then led his division out from Wei Province and crossed Wulan ford to the northwest.

literal: Yuwen Tai repeatedly sent troops to intercept him; whenever Yuan fought he crushed them.
idiomatic: Yuwen Tai repeatedly sent troops to intercept him; whenever Yuan fought he crushed them.

literal: He led his army through the territories of He and Yuan provinces, and only then got out eastward.
idiomatic: He led his army through the territories of He and Yuan provinces and only then broke out eastward.

literal: Inspector of Lingzhou Cao Qi had a son-in-law Liu Feng who was deeply connected with Yuan; Yuan therefore persuaded Feng that Gao Huan was extraordinarily heroic and would accomplish great enterprise; from then on Feng had the heart to submit his allegiance, and supplied Yuan for his journey.
idiomatic: Inspector of Lingzhou Cao Qi had a son-in-law, Liu Feng, who was deeply connected with Yuan; Yuan therefore persuaded Feng that Gao Huan was extraordinarily heroic and would accomplish great enterprise; from then on Feng had the heart to pledge allegiance, and supplied Yuan for his journey.

literal: Yuan entered Yun Province from the northeast of Lingzhou.
idiomatic: Yuan entered Yun Province from the northeast of Lingzhou.

literal: When Gao Huan heard he was coming, he sent Administrator of Pingyang Gao Song with a gold ring to bestow on Yuan, and shipped provisions, sending envoys far to meet him.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan heard he was coming, he sent the administrator of Pingyang, Gao Song, with a gold ring to bestow on Yuan, shipped provisions, and sent envoys far ahead to meet him.

literal: When Yuan reached Jinyang, he was received in audience and they clasped hands; he was given a thousand bolts of silk plus slaves, maidservants, fields and houses.
idiomatic: When Yuan reached Jinyang he was received in audience and they clasped hands; he was given a thousand bolts of silk together with slaves, maidservants, fields, and houses.

literal: His four brothers who were earlier in Bingzhou were promoted in rank and enfeoffment.
idiomatic: His four brothers who were already in Bingzhou were promoted in rank and enfeoffment.

literal: All the commanders and generals of Yuan's division were rewarded with ranks and fiefs.
idiomatic: All the commanders and generals of Yuan's division were rewarded with ranks and fiefs.

literal: Yuan was enfeoffed Duke of a county and appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
idiomatic: Yuan was enfeoffed duke of a county and appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry.

literal: He attacked Western Wei yitong Jin Zuo and Huangfu Zhida at Dongyong and captured them.
idiomatic: He attacked Western Wei yitong Jin Zuo and Huangfu Zhida at Dongyong and captured them.

literal: He was transferred to inspector of Bingzhou.
idiomatic: He was transferred to inspector of Bingzhou.

literal: Again with the generals on campaigns, he had repeated victories in subduing foes.
idiomatic: Again campaigning with the generals, he had repeated victories in subduing foes.

literal: Early in Tianbao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Fufeng.
idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he was enfeoffed prince of Fufeng.

literal: He repeatedly followed Gao Yang in campaigns against the Shanhu and Ruru, with repeated battle merit.
idiomatic: He repeatedly followed Gao Yang in campaigns against the Shanhu and Ruru and won repeated battle merit.

literal: He was transferred to Grand Preceptor and died.
idiomatic: He was transferred to grand preceptor and died.

literal: Posthumously given the yellow axe of authority, Grand Tutor, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was given the yellow axe of authority, grand tutor, and recorder of the masters of writing.

literal: Yuan was skilled at governing troops; in marching and using troops he always aimed at steadiness; in front and rear expeditions he never suffered defeat.
idiomatic: Yuan was skilled at governing troops; in marching and using troops he always aimed at steadiness; in expedition after expedition he never suffered defeat.

literal: When he died the court deeply mourned him.
idiomatic: When he died the court deeply mourned him.

literal: Early in Huangjian, he was granted joint sacrifice in Gao Cheng's temple hall.
idiomatic: Early in Huangjian he was granted joint sacrifice in Gao Cheng's temple hall.

literal: Liu Feng, styled Fengsheng, was a native of Pule.
idiomatic: Liu Feng, styled Fengsheng, came from Pule.

literal: He had heroic bearing and stalwart spirit, resolution surpassing others, was eloquent of speech, and loved to discuss military affairs.
idiomatic: He had heroic bearing and stalwart spirit, resolution surpassing others, was eloquent, and loved to discuss military affairs.

literal: In Poliuhan Baling's rebellion, Feng for merit in holding the city was appointed Administrator of Pule.
idiomatic: In Poliuhan Baling's rebellion, Feng for merit in holding the city was appointed administrator of Pule.
